semantics.clock: Transitions at rising edges of clk; conventional FSM edge interpretation for the specified clk input.
semantics.reset: Active-high asynchronous areset forces OFF, as explicitly stated in problem.txt; reset dominates clock transitions while asserted.

transitions.OFF: j=0 holds OFF; j=1 enters ON; k irrelevant
transitions.ON: k=0 holds ON; k=1 enters OFF; j irrelevant

semantics.output: OFF gives out=0; ON gives out=1, directly decoded from current state without extra latency.
semantics.initialization: No power-up state is specified; no initialized register or pre-reset output guarantee is added.
semantics.reset_release: Deassertion alone causes no transition; next rising clock edge samples the inputs.

numeric.port_widths: All ports are one bit as specified

verification.oracle_basis: Original problem.txt transition diagram and asynchronous reset statement
verification.sampling: Observe out after NBA settling at rising edges; also verify stability between clock edges and asynchronous reset response away from edges.
verification.directed: All four j,k combinations from each state, repeated transitions, irrelevant-input changes, held reset, reset from ON, reset release with j asserted.
verification.checks: Self-checking dev_tb with fatal mismatches, bounded timeout and final PASS; run unchanged dev_check.py --label initial.
verification.scope: Development simulation only; no official evaluation or synthesis.

specification_ambiguities.evidence: Problem specifies clk and FSM but does not explicitly name an edge
Only reset-to-OFF and binary transitions are specified
specification_ambiguities.interpretation: Do not impose pre-reset or X/Z-input behavior in the oracle
